spec.title: codkit PROP-002: Code layout, launch, toolchain, components

status.comment: the layout of standalone Codkit with independent toolRoot, patchesDir and forkDir

layout.title: 1. Where the code lives

p.layout-lead: The layout is split into three roots which may live on different disks and may not coincide, nest inside one another, or be derived from one another:

layout.fence:
workspaceRoot/ the tool repository: a private npm workspace that publishes nothing package.json the workspace root (`workspaces: ["packages/*"]`) and the development toolchain npm-shrinkwrap.json the locked development install of the whole workspace bin/codkit, bin/codkit.ps1 the source-checkout launchers over the CLI package packages/** one directory per published package: the CLI and the project types (PROP-016 §3) tools/**, docs/** the repository's own generators, gates and documentation vibevm/vibespecs/** the normative specs of the tool conform.toml, specmap.toml the structural and traceability policy of the repository
toolRoot = packages/codkit/ the immutable installation of Codkit: the CLI package package.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json dependencies and the version of the tool bin/codkit, bin/codkit.ps1 user-facing Bash/PowerShell launchers bin/codkit.mjs the internal Node launcher src/** production TypeScript dist/** deterministic runtime JavaScript config/** the mandatory safety policy and the default build-watch data test/** unit/e2e claude/**, hooks/** the agent-session profile a product installs and its pre-tool guard (FEAT-004) vibevm/vibepacks/** the shipped vibe packages (the standards package, PROP-014) runtime/** the shipped runtime library (PROP-015), one directory per version
patchesDir/ the consumer's external Git work tree codkit.json the pin and the parameters of this patch set codkit.local.json local non-pin overrides delta/** own/patches/overlays/resources/rules/removed/owners cycle/** the committed state and journal of the upgrade cycle .codkit/** local locks/cache/logs/generated output vibe.toml the manifest of the product's vibevm project; the codkit:begin/end standards block (PROP-014 §4) vibevm/vibepacks/** the installed copy of the standards package (PROP-014 §5), owned by codkit delta/own/codkit/** the installed runtime library and the copy of the notice (PROP-015 §4), owned by codkit delta/own-extensions/** the product's built-in extensions as own-extension units (PROP-005 §13)
forkDir/ the external managed VS Code checkout .git/** upstream objects, generated refs and local marks/hooks src/**, product.json, ... the materialized working state

facts.ROOT-OWNERSHIP: toolRoot is the CLI package `packages/codkit` of the tool's npm workspace, and only it owns the sources, the launchers, the base safety configs, the tests and the npm dependencies of Codkit; the workspace root above it owns the repository's own machinery (the specs, the generators, the gates, the development lock) and is private - it publishes nothing. Only patchesDir owns `codkit.json`, `delta/**`, `cycle/**`, the runtime `.codkit/**` and the Git history of the patch set. Only forkDir owns the VS Code checkout and the generated refs. The standards package in toolRoot belongs to toolRoot; its installed copy under patchesDir belongs to codkit and is edited only by the standards load command (PROP-014).
facts.PATCHSET-GITIGNORE: A patch set ignores at least `codkit.local.json` and `.codkit/`. It is not obliged to have a `package.json` or `node_modules` for the sake of Codkit.
facts.TOOL-PACKAGE: `package.json` and the publishable `npm-shrinkwrap.json` belong to toolRoot - that is, to the CLI package `packages/codkit`, not to the workspace root - and fix the runtime dependency graph identically in the source checkout and in the npm artifact. The workspace root carries its own `npm-shrinkwrap.json` for the development install of every package at once; it is never published. The runtime dependencies are installed next to the tool. Missing dependencies give a diagnosed refusal that demands the installation be restored from the approved supply; for a source checkout `npm ci` is admissible.
facts.TOOL-PACKAGE-TAR-BOUND: Bounds of the npm tarball in `packages/codkit/test/unit/packageManifest.test.ts`, applied to every published package of the workspace (PROP-016 ##TYPE-SUPPLY-KIT): the test packs each `packages/*` with `npm pack --dry-run` and states, per package, the files it must ship, the executables it must keep executable, and these bounds. **Decision (owner ruling, 2026-09-07, verbatim: «поднять размер в тесте до 50 мегабайт»):** `unpackedSize < 50_000_000`; `entryCount < 640` and the tar bound `2_000_000` stay as the ruling of 2026-09-06 left them. **Why:** the unpacked bound fired on planned work - the STANDARDS campaign added the standards package (81_940 bytes), PROP-014 (112_670) and six modules that ship twice, as sources and as their compiled output, taking the tarball to 5_055_081 unpacked with the tar at 1_383_894 and 429 of 640 entries. Nothing a consumer experiences was near a limit: 5 MB unpacked on a developer machine costs nothing, and this decision's own revisit trigger (the tar above 2 MB, or a consumer complaint) had not fired. A ratchet that blocks planned work without naming a cost measures the wrong thing. The consequence is recorded rather than hidden: at this number the effective ratchet is the tar bound, which text compressing about fivefold reaches near 10 MB unpacked, so 50 MB is never approached - the unpacked bound is now a backstop against a pathological artifact, not the growth signal. **Consequence of the workspace split (2026-09-09):** a package can only ship what lies inside it, so the CLI tarball carries the runnable tool and the operator surfaces that live in `packages/codkit` - the sources, the compiled runtime, the launchers, the configs, the agent profile and its guard, the shipped vibe packages and the runtime library - while the repository's specifications, `docs/codkit` and the repository-level `AUDIT.md`/`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` stay at the workspace root and reach a consumer through the repository rather than through the tarball. **Considered and rejected:** dropping `packages/codkit/src` from the shipped set - measured at 272 entries and 3_063_152 unpacked, and the launcher runs `packages/codkit/dist/main.js` so sources are not needed at runtime, but a consumer would stop receiving the source of the tool they installed, and that is a distribution decision nobody asked for; a smaller step such as 5_500_000 - the owner named 50 MB; dropping `AUDIT.md` or `docs/codkit` - documentation a consumer should have. **When to revisit:** the tar exceeds 2 MB (unchanged, and now the binding signal), or a consumer reports install size or time.
facts.ROOT-DERIVATION: toolRoot is computed only from the `import.meta.url` of the tool being launched. patchesDir and forkDir are resolved independently through the sources of PROP-003; cwd never becomes a root automatically.

facts.COMPILED-RUNTIME-LAUNCHER: The source of truth is the TypeScript in `packages/codkit/src`. `npm run runtime:build` produces plain ESM JavaScript in `packages/codkit/dist` with rewritten relative extensions; `runtime:check` compares a fresh temp emit with the tracked dist byte for byte. The launcher calls `node toolRoot/dist/main.js <args>` with the same `process.execPath`, so an installed npm package does not try to strip `.ts` under `node_modules`.
facts.USER-LAUNCHERS: The user entry points are `bin/codkit` for Bash and `bin/codkit.ps1` for PowerShell. They exist twice and identically in purpose: inside the CLI package, where an installation is rooted, and at the workspace root of the source checkout. Both resolve the root relative to their own file (not to cwd), check that Node is available and pass argv and the exit code on to the internal `bin/codkit.mjs` of the CLI package; the wrapper scripts carry no command or format logic.
facts.ERASABLE-SYNTAX-ONLY: A constraint for the codkit code: erasable TS syntax only — no `enum`, no `namespace`, no constructor parameter properties; instead of an enum — union types and `as const` objects. (It coincides with the `erasableSyntaxOnly` flag of the AI-native TypeScript envelope — `common/PROP-000` §5.)
facts.NODE-VERSION-RULE: Codkit itself requires Node ≥ 22.6 as its installed runtime floor. The build version of a particular fork is set by that fork's `.nvmrc`; if the resolved tree requires another major, Codkit warns instead of substituting the environment, and it does not make a consumer-specific version part of the tool policy.
facts.GIT-VERSION-RULE: git ≥ 2.40 (a stable `git apply`, `merge-file`, `commit-tree` and `--force-with-lease` are needed); git-lfs ≥ 3.0 is an environment contract: without it the tree holds pointer files.
facts.CROSS-PLATFORM-PATHS: The operating systems: Linux, macOS, Windows. All paths go through `node:path`/`node:fs` (`realpath`), never through concatenation of strings with separators; on Windows codkit checks `core.longpaths=true` in the config of the tree and warns when it is absent.

p.PUBLIC-ROOT-SOURCES: `CODKIT_PATCHES_DIR` and `CODKIT_FORK_DIR` are public user sources, not test overrides. Each root has its own independent precedence CLI flag → env → `~/.codkit/settings.json`; relative CLI and env paths are resolved from cwd, and settings accepts absolute paths only.

p.GIT-ENV-ISOLATION: **The isolation of the Git environment is the foundation of determinism:** every git run from codkit is executed with the environment `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `LC_ALL=C`, `TZ=UTC` and with explicit `-c core.autocrlf=false -c core.eol=lf -c core.quotepath=false` (the line ending: `##GIT-ENV-EOL` below); the repository settings that are needed are passed as `-c` flags. The exceptions are the operations obliged to see the config of the repository or of the container (reading `safe.directory` in CI, PROP-011 §5; their list is fixed there) and the single read-only query `rev-parse --git-path hooks/<name>` with the machine config visible (the `machineConfig` flag of the wrapper, legal ONLY together with `pathResolution`): the effective location of a configured hook is a property of the user's git, an isolated view does not see it, and to declare the guard active without asking the user's git would be a lie (PROP-008 §3 `##TREE-HOOK-STEP`, REPAIR-006).

p.GIT-HOOK-NULL-SINK: Isolated Git executions suppress repository hooks with core.hooksPath=NUL on native Windows and core.hooksPath=/dev/null on POSIX. Git LFS filter-process may attempt automatic hook installation; the Windows sink must not turn into a literal dev/null directory inside the checkout. Explicit clone setup uses git lfs install --local --skip-repo to configure filters without installing disabled hooks. Clean/smudge filters remain enabled, exact LFS pointer/content checks remain intact, and unowned/dirty files are never ignored or deleted to make a workspace clean. Path-resolution/machine-config queries and gitLocal human commits retain their existing exceptions. This changes no stored protocol, policy permissions, user repository config or installed type receipt.

p.GIT-ENV-EOL: **The line ending a checkout writes is not a platform default.** `core.autocrlf=false` keeps the machine's configuration out of the bytes git writes, but not the platform: for a file the tree's attributes mark as text (upstream VS Code declares `* text=auto`), the line ending a checkout writes is `core.eol`, whose default `native` is CRLF on Windows and LF everywhere else. That is how a fork tree on Windows came to hold CRLF where the applied branch stores the patch set's LF (`git ls-files --eol`: `i/lf w/crlf`): the checkout with which `load` moves the tree onto a new tip (PROP-008 §3) and the one with which `package` puts back the overlay targets and the packager's scratch paths wrote every text file they touched with CRLF, where the same run on Linux writes LF, and a package built from that working copy - a Linux one built on Windows too, with its `*.desktop`, `debian/control` and `rpm` spec templates - carried the CRLF. Every git run from codkit therefore also carries `-c core.eol=lf`: a checkout by codkit writes a text file with the blob's line endings on every OS, which is what a checkout on Linux writes. It is a flag of codkit's own command lines, not configuration written into the tree: a checkout codkit does not make is not affected, and the user's own git in the fork tree keeps its settings. It changes what a checkout writes and nothing that git reads: a working file is normalized the same way before `status`, `diff` or `hash-object` compare it, so the drift guard sees what it saw before. The tree's own declarations for a path still hold, and identically on every OS: `eol=crlf` on upstream's `*.bat`, `*.cmd` and licence texts makes a checkout write CRLF on Linux as well. For a file the delta writes, PROP-008 `##WORKTREE-DELTA-BYTES` makes the bytes exact whatever the attributes say, and says how a tree written before this rule heals. The advice codkit gives where it finds a carriage return in a file it reads (`CK-E-CRLF`) names both settings for the same reason: after `core.autocrlf=false` alone, the user's own checkout on Windows writes the CRLF again. A tree already written that way is found before the work it would waste: the materialization of the upgrade cycle (PROP-009) proves every file it moves byte for byte, and a working copy with CRLF over an LF blob fails that proof - after the build of the prospective tree, which on a large upstream takes minutes - while `git status` is clean over it, because git's stat cache calls the file unchanged. So the cycle asks first, with `git ls-files --eol`, which reads the working copies: a tracked file with `i/lf` and `w/crlf` (or `w/mixed`) whose attributes do not ask for `eol=crlf` is `CK-E-CRLF` before anything is built, with the paths and the recipe (both settings, then `git checkout-index --force` over the listed paths, which rewrites them from the index and nothing else). The proof of the move gives the same answer for a file it finds in that state on a resume: a copy that equals the recorded bytes once its CRLF read as LF is named as such, with the file's recipe instead of the transaction's.

p.CONTAINED-FILE-IO: **The administrative files touched by REPAIR-006 (the git mark, the hooks, the exclude) and the configuration reads of `codkit.json` / `codkit.local.json` / the declared build-watch and conventions all go through one implementation, `containedFile.ts`.** Reading: the parent components are checked with lstat (a symbolic link is a refusal), the leaf is opened with a single descriptor with `O_NOFOLLOW` (the platforms without it — Windows — check the leaf before the open and compare the descriptor afterwards; the remaining check-then-open window is documented, not hidden), the descriptor must be a regular file, and after the open it is proved that it names a file inside the root (realpath + a comparison of dev/ino with the canonical path) — a parent component swapped for a symlink after the check is caught by the post-open proof and its bytes are not used. Writing: an atomic replacement (an exclusive temporary file + rename) only inside a parent which, immediately before the write, must be a real canonical directory; a leaf symlink is a refusal (`codkit never writes through a link`), and a symlink swapped in after the check of the leaf is replaced by the rename itself — the target of the link does not change; after the write the identity and realpath of the parent are re-checked. On Windows a rename refused because another handle holds the target open is tried again within a bounded budget before it refuses (`##CONTAINED-WINDOWS-REPLACE-RETRY`). The limitation of the Node `fs` is recorded honestly: the portable API gives no `openat`/`renameat` relative to a held directory descriptor, so a malicious swap of the parent itself in the narrow window between the last check and the creation of the temporary file is detected post-write but is not prevented before the first byte on every platform; a pre-existing parent or leaf symlink and a swap during a read are refused before the data is used. The administrative directories (`hooks/`, `codkit/`, `info/`) are created only as real directories — a symlink component is a refusal. The module does not decide «whose bytes these are»: ownership and refusal stay with the calling layer.

p.CONTAINED-WINDOWS-REPLACE-RETRY: **On Windows the rename of an atomic replacement waits for another handle on its target to close, within a bounded budget, and then refuses exactly as before.** Windows refuses to rename a file over a target that any other handle holds open: Node's rename there does not use the POSIX rename semantics. Measured on 2026-09-24 (Node 24.18, Windows 11): a handle on the target in another process - of any sharing mode, one that allows deletion and a plain Node read included - makes `renameSync(temporary, target)` fail with `EPERM`; a handle without delete sharing on the temporary makes it fail with `EBUSY`; a handle that allows deletion on the temporary does not stop it. Such a holder is not codkit's to close: the one measured on a file written moments before was a kernel-mode handle (PROP-010 `##DAEMON-RECORD-REPLACE-BUDGET` has the measurements). So on `win32`, and only there, a replacement whose rename fails with `EPERM`, `EACCES`, `EBUSY` or `ENOTEMPTY` is tried again after a wait: the first wait is 10 ms, each next one doubles, no wait is longer than 250 ms, and no wait is taken that would bring the sum of the waits above the budget of the write. The default budget, the one every contained atomic write gets, is 310 ms: waits of 10, 20, 40, 80 and 160 ms, six attempts in all - a rename refused five times succeeds on its sixth attempt, one refused six times refuses. A caller that replaces a file it published moments before names a longer budget of its own; the pid transition of a daemon record is the one that does (PROP-010 `##DAEMON-RECORD-REPLACE-BUDGET`). The retry never removes the target first: until a rename succeeds, the previous bytes stay under the name. When the budget is spent, the answer is the refusal a failed rename has always been - `CK-E-CONFIG` `<what>: cannot atomically replace <path>: <errno message>` with the hint `check the permissions of the parent directory`, and the temporary removed. A real permission error therefore still refuses: on Windows once the budget is spent, since a denied rename and a held target both report `EPERM`, and at the first failure for any other errno and on every other platform. The tests drive the retry through the seams `applyRename`, `renamePlatform` and `waitForRenameRetry` of the atomic write (`containedFileWindowsRetry.test.ts`).

p.CONTAINED-CONSUMERS: REPAIR-007: the tree mark, the common/worktree exclude, the tree hook and the patch-set hooks use `readContainedFile(root, relative)` end-to-end, and the writes use `writeContainedFileAtomic`; a checked parent is not then handed to a weaker leaf-only reader. On a real FS `writeConfigPin` reads descriptor-held bytes, performs a repeated contained CAS read and writes a contained atomic replacement; the injectable legacy FS stays a test seam only. Every public consumer has a deterministic after-open parent-swap regression with an unchanged outside sentinel.

p.CONFIG-PIN-CAPABILITY: REPAIR-009: mutating the pin in `codkit.json` requires a LIVE capability of this patch set's cycle-global lock, not merely a structurally similar handle: a forged, a copied, an already released and a foreign (another patchesDir) handle all refuse. The bytes are re-read before the replacement, so an external edit that arrived after the comparison is preserved and the call returns a locked/config failure. The residual limitation is recorded honestly: an external editor whose last system call writes after our repeated read can still be overwritten — Node gives no atomic compare-and-swap over an ordinary file.

p.components-lead: The file names are a recommendation, the responsibilities are normative:

td.COMP-PATHS-RESP: the independent resolver of patchesDir/forkDir, canonicalization, the disjoint-root guard, printing of the sources

td.COMP-TREE-IDENTITY-RESP: the checks of the identity and the fitness of the tree

td.COMP-GITX-RESP: the wrapper that runs git with environment isolation (§2), parsing of the output, the `netAllowed` flag

td.COMP-LAYERS-RESP: one module per delta layer: own, patch, overlay, resource, entry, rule

td.COMP-MARKERS-RESP: the parser and validator of markers per language

td.COMP-PATCH-FORMAT-RESP: reading and writing of `.ckpatch`, normalization of the diff

td.COMP-APPLY-ENGINE-RESP: the application loop over the artifacts, classification of the outcomes; dry-run

td.COMP-SYNC: A tombstone (Phase 1 of the TREE-COMMITS-SAVE campaign, 2026-09-06): replaced by `COMP-LOAD`; the address is unchanged (NEVER-RENAME-OR-DELETE-A-CITED-ANCHOR).

td.COMP-SYNC-RESP: A tombstone (the same phase): replaced by `COMP-LOAD-RESP`.

td.COMP-LOAD-RESP: `load`: bringing the tree to the pin, building the branch, the mtime discipline

td.COMP-SAVE-RESP: `save`/extract: mirroring of own, regeneration of the patches

td.COMP-INVENTORY-RESP: generation of the inventory, the checks, the diff, the metrics

td.COMP-FINGERPRINT-RESP: the fingerprints of the delta and of the tree, the application cache

td.COMP-LOCK-RESP: the file lock over the tree

td.COMP-BUILD-WRAP-RESP: the wrapper of the watch daemons

td.COMP-CYCLE-RESP: the orchestrator: the state, the phases, the classification, the journal

td.COMP-CAUSE-RESP: the search for the upstream commit that is the cause

td.COMP-OVERLAY-ENGINE-RESP: application and verification of a config-overlay

td.COMP-PUBLISH-RESP: assembling and pushing of the generated refs

td.COMP-HOOKS-RESP: installation and verification of the Git hooks of the patch set and of the tree

td.COMP-JSON-OUT-RESP: the `--json` envelope, the registry of message codes

td.COMP-LICENSE-CHECK-MODULES-RESP: the policy, the canonical UPL text and the check of the licence annotation of the package

td.COMP-STANDARDS-MODULES-RESP: the standards package in toolRoot, the managed block of `vibe.toml`, the `standards load|check` engine

td.COMP-RUNTIME-MODULES-RESP: the runtime library in toolRoot, the `runtime load|check` engine, the delivered files

td.COMP-GEN-MODULES-RESP: the skeletons of a feature and of the brand tables in the product's own

td.COMP-FAKE-TREE-RESP: the fake fork tree for the tests

p.DEPENDENCY-RULE-BETWEEN-MODULES: `layers/*`, `applyEngine` and `inventory` know nothing about the CLI; the commands receive explicit toolRoot, patchesDir, forkDir and the patch-set config object instead of reopening the roots through cwd. This is the cell rule of AI-native TypeScript as well: one module = one cell with a single public entry.

cross-platform.title: 4. Cross-platform support — the conditions of acceptance

facts.XPLAT-DOUBLE-REGEN: Acceptance requires a native test «a double regeneration gives an empty diff» separately on Linux, macOS and Windows (S16). The current Linux run is not a proof for the two other operating systems.
facts.XPLAT-NO-NEIGHBOR-ASSUMPTION: No mechanism assumes that the three roots are neighbours; the tests use three unrelated random paths (PROP-013 §1).
facts.XPLAT-NO-SYMLINKS: Symlinks are not used as a mechanism (code is delivered by copying); on Windows linking is replaced by a copy everywhere.
